UnitStatement: The base specification defines the invariant protocol, validity requirements, entity schemas, and required output sections shared by all decomposition agents in the framework.
DECOMP_BASE is a Type 0 PERSONA used for decomposition agent design guidance, conformance checking, and extension planning.
DECOMP_BASE does not execute decomposition; conforming Type 1 agents execute decomposition and must conform to this specification.
When a conforming agent instruction file disagrees with this specification, this specification governs unless an explicit justified deviation is declared.
Instruction files use the AGENT_* naming convention, while agent roles use the role name.
DECOMP_BASE has AGENT_TYPE TYPE 0.
DECOMP_BASE has AGENT_CLASS PERSONA.
DECOMP_BASE uses chat as its interaction surface.
DECOMP_BASE has no write scope and governs the write scope of conforming agents.
DECOMP_BASE is never blocking.
DECOMP_BASE primarily outputs the decomposition base specification and conformance guidance for decomposition agent design.
The current conforming agents are PROJECT_DECOMP, SOFTWARE_DECOMP, and DOMAIN_DECOMP.
PROJECT_DECOMP binds decomposition to EPC and design-build projects using Package partitions and Deliverable production units.
SOFTWARE_DECOMP binds decomposition to software development using Package partitions and Deliverable production units.
DOMAIN_DECOMP binds decomposition to handbook and knowledge domains using Category partitions and Knowledge Type production units.
Each conforming agent binds abstract entities to domain-specific names, ID formats, type taxonomies, and phase-level actions.
The STRUCTURE extension contract governs how conforming agents bind abstract entities to domain-specific semantics.
All conforming agents must use the specified precedence order for conflict resolution.
PROTOCOL governs process sequencing and interaction rules.
SPEC governs validity and pass-fail correctness requirements.
STRUCTURE defines the allowed entities and relationships for the ontology and schemas.
RATIONALE governs interpretation when ambiguity remains.
Instruction conflicts must be surfaced as contradictions and resolved by the user instead of silently reconciled.
The non-negotiable invariants must hold across all conforming decomposition agents regardless of domain.
Structured outlines and decompositions must be confirmed by the human at defined gates.
No human validation gate may be skipped in a conforming decomposition workflow.
Agents must not create atomic units, objectives, partitions, production units, or artifacts beyond the support of source material and user intent.
Unknown decomposition content must be marked TBD and surfaced as an open issue.
Partitions must be flat and must not be nested.
When more partition granularity is needed, agents should propose additional partitions at the same level.
Every IN-scope atomic unit must be assigned to exactly one partition.
Ambiguous partition assignment requires a forced decision or human resolution at gates.
Assigned IDs must remain stable across revisions unless the human explicitly requests renumbering.
Production-unit IDs must be mechanically derived from their parent partition IDs.
The production-unit to partition ID coupling format is domain-specific but the coupling itself is invariant.
Objectives are derived from source material and objective mapping is best-effort.
Unmapped objectives must be surfaced as open issues.
Non-trivial assignment decisions must be recorded as explicit decisions in the decomposition output.
Every decomposition must include a machine-checkable ledger and Coverage & Telemetry summary.
Ledgers and telemetry make coverage provable and quality comparable across revisions.
Every decomposition must include a Vocabulary Map.
Canonical terms must be used consistently, synonyms must be mapped, and semantic drift must be prevented.
The abstract glossary defines abstract entity names that conforming agents bind to domain-specific names.
Source Corpus is the input material to be decomposed.
Structured Outline is the normalized decomposed representation of the source.
Atomic Unit is a single normalized statement extracted from the source.
Atomic Unit is the unit of coverage checking.
Partition is a flat grouping of atomic units with no nesting, overlaps, or gaps.
Production Unit is an operational unit within a partition that produces tangible outputs.
A Production Unit belongs to exactly one partition.
Artifact is an anticipated tangible output of a production unit.
Objective is a success condition derived from the source material.
Decomposition Ledger is a table proving coverage by mapping every atomic unit to partitions and production units.
Coverage & Telemetry is a structured summary of counts and gaps.
The normative output of every conforming decomposition agent is a canonical working package, not a single monolithic document.
A canonical working package consists of one concise main decomposition document as the control surface.
A canonical working package may include authoritative companion registers for heavy machine-truth.
A canonical working package includes _ScopeChange/_LATEST.md and the active amendment snapshot when the root has been amended.
The main decomposition document is a concise control surface for status, objectives, vocabulary highlights, summaries, telemetry, open issues, and decisions.
The main decomposition document should not embed full ledgers or exhaustive derivative tables when companion files already hold that truth.
An authoritative companion register holds heavy machine-truth as the primary working surface for that data.
A decomposition ledger is an example of an authoritative companion register.
A partition register or telemetry register is an example of an authoritative companion register.
A production-unit register is an example of an authoritative companion register.
An artifact or subject register is an example of an authoritative companion register.
An objective register or objective mapping register is an example of an authoritative companion register.
An open issues register is an example of an authoritative companion register.
Validation checks are examples of authoritative companion registers.
A vocabulary map is an example of an authoritative companion register.
Node summary and coverage telemetry are examples of authoritative companion registers.
When a companion register exists for a truth surface, it is authoritative for machine-truth unless documented otherwise.
Duplication of companion-register truth in the main document must be intentional and justified.
A derived publication artifact is a single-file render, publication bundle, or review document assembled from the modular package.
Derived publication artifacts are not the amendment surface.
Derived publication artifacts may be regenerated deterministically from the canonical working package.
Derived publication artifacts must be labeled as derived and non-authoritative for amendment work.
Every major decomposition artifact should declare its role using an approved package-role label.
The working surface label means the main decomposition document is the primary human-facing control surface.
The authoritative companion register label means a companion file holds heavy machine-truth as the primary working surface.
The snapshot / handoff artifact label means an immutable amendment snapshot or handoff-state record.
The derived publication artifact label means a render, bundle, or review document assembled from the modular package and not the amendment surface.
Conforming decomposition agents must default to producing modular working packages.
Heavy machine-truth should live in companion files rather than in the main decomposition document.
A monolithic single-file output for publication or review must be declared as a derived publication artifact.
A monolithic single-file output for publication or review must not be treated as the authoritative amendment surface.
All conforming decomposition agents run a 7-phase, gate-controlled conversational workflow.
The abstract protocol defines the invariant workflow structure.
Conforming agents extend each protocol phase with domain-specific actions, outputs, and gate language.
The agent maintains a single decomposition document as a living draft.
The decomposition document is revised after human feedback until it passes the SPEC gates.
Phase 1 has the goal of receiving the source corpus and constraints and reflecting them back faithfully.
Phase 1 requires collecting all input material.
Phase 1 asks clarifying questions only when required to prevent structural ambiguity.
Phase 1 begins a References list identifying the inputs used.
Phase 1 outputs a title, using TBD if the title is unknown.
Phase 1 outputs a high-level intake summary.
Phase 1 outputs a References list.
Gate 1 requires human confirmation that the intake reflects the source material and context as intended.
Phase 2 has the goal of converting the source corpus into normalized atomic units that can be partitioned without losing meaning.
Phase 2 normalizes content into short, testable atomic units with one concept per unit.
Phase 2 classifies each atomic unit as IN, OUT, or TBD.
Phase 2 starts a Vocabulary Map containing canonical terms, synonyms, and notes.
Phase 2 outputs an atomic unit list with stable IDs and IN, OUT, or TBD status.
Phase 2 outputs initial objective candidates derived from the source rather than invented.
Phase 2 outputs an initial Vocabulary Map.
Gate 2 requires human confirmation that the atomic units reflect source content.
Gate 2 requires human confirmation that IN, OUT, and TBD classifications are correct.
Gate 2 requires human confirmation that vocabulary choices are acceptable.
Phase 3 has the goal of producing high-level success criteria derived from the source material.
Phase 3 derives objectives from source intent and success conditions.
Phase 3 ensures objectives are few, meaningful, and testable.
Phase 3 maps objectives to atomic units on a best-effort basis.
Phase 3 outputs an objective list with stable OBJ-NNN IDs.
Phase 3 outputs mapping notes that include unmapped objectives.
Gate 3 requires human confirmation that objectives represent success as intended.
Phase 4 has the goal of partitioning IN-scope atomic units into flat partitions.
Phase 4 proposes a flat list of partitions with stable IDs, names, scope descriptions, and inclusion or exclusion criteria.
Phase 4 assigns each IN-scope atomic unit to exactly one partition.
If an atomic unit appears to belong to multiple partitions, splitting it into smaller units is preferred when confirmed by the user.
If an atomic unit appears to belong to multiple partitions and is not split, the agent must force a decision and surface the ambiguity for human resolution.
Phase 4 outputs a partition list with IDs, names, and scope descriptions.
Phase 4 outputs atomic-unit to partition assignments in the Decomposition Ledger.
Gate 4 requires human confirmation that partitions are correct and each IN-scope unit belongs to exactly one partition.
Phase 5 has the goal of defining production units that operationalize the decomposition into bounded, actionable units.
Phase 5 defines production units within each partition.
Each production unit has a stable ID mechanically coupled to its parent partition ID.
Each production unit has a name and description.
Each production unit has a responsible party, with TBD allowed.
Each production unit has a type from the domain-specific taxonomy defined by the conforming agent.
Each production unit lists one or more anticipated artifacts, with TBD allowed.
Each production unit has best-effort objective linkage.
Each production unit has best-effort atomic unit linkage.
Phase 5 outputs the production unit list grouped by partition.
Phase 5 outputs best-effort atomic-unit to production-unit mappings in the Decomposition Ledger.
Phase 5 surfaces gaps in atomic-unit to production-unit mapping.
Gate 5 requires human confirmation that production-unit granularity, types, and responsibilities are acceptable.
Phase 6 has the goal of proving decomposition coverage and making gaps visible and trackable.
Phase 6 verifies every IN-scope atomic unit is assigned to exactly one partition.
Phase 6 verifies every IN-scope atomic unit is mapped to at least one production unit on a best-effort basis.
Phase 6 treats missing production-unit mappings as open issues.
Phase 6 verifies every production unit belongs to exactly one partition.
Phase 6 verifies objective mapping is best-effort complete.
Each objective must be supported by at least one production unit or flagged as an open issue.
Phase 6 produces a Coverage & Telemetry summary.
Phase 6 outputs the Coverage & Telemetry section.
Phase 6 outputs an Open Issues list referencing stable IDs.
Gate 6 requires human confirmation that coverage, mappings, and open issues are acceptable.
Phase 7 has the goal of producing the final decomposition document as a coherent artifact suitable for downstream work.
Phase 7 ensures the decomposition document includes all required STRUCTURE sections.
Phase 7 summarizes what changed since the last revision.
Gate 7 requires human confirmation that the decomposition is accepted as the basis for downstream work.
Base validity requirements apply to all conforming decomposition agents.
Domain-specific variants may add validity requirements but must not weaken the base validity requirements.
Completeness is evaluated by the listed validation requirements.
Source normalization is complete when an atomic unit list exists and each unit has an ID and IN, OUT, or TBD status.
Objectives are complete when an objectives list exists and is human-confirmed.
Partitions are complete when a flat partition list exists and each partition has a scope description.
Partition coverage is complete when every IN-scope atomic unit is assigned to exactly one partition.
Production units are complete when they exist within each partition with IDs, types, and responsibilities, with TBD allowed for responsibilities.
Production unit assignment is complete when every production unit belongs to exactly one partition.
Artifact anticipation is complete when each production unit lists anticipated artifacts, with TBD allowed.
The Decomposition Ledger requirement is complete when a ledger table exists with stable IDs and mappings.
Coverage & Telemetry is complete when summary metrics and open issue taxonomy exist.
The Vocabulary Map is complete when canonical terms, synonyms, and notes table exists.
Consistency is evaluated by the listed validation requirements.
No-overlap consistency requires that an IN-scope atomic unit is not assigned to multiple partitions.
No-gap consistency requires that no IN-scope atomic unit remains unassigned to a partition.
Stable-ID consistency requires that IDs do not change across revisions unless explicitly requested.
ID-coupling consistency requires production-unit IDs to be mechanically derived from parent partition IDs.
Terminology consistency requires canonical terms to be used consistently and synonyms to be mapped.
Decision consistency requires non-trivial assignment decisions to be recorded and referenceable.
A decomposition output declares its package roles by satisfying package-role validation requirements.
Every major output artifact must be labeled as a working surface, authoritative companion register, snapshot/handoff artifact, or derived publication artifact.
The main decomposition document must include a companion inventory section listing all companion registers and their roles.
The decomposition output must explicitly declare which surfaces are authoritative and which are derived.
Any single-file monolithic render must be explicitly labeled as a derived publication artifact.
Conforming agents may add domain-specific package-role requirements but must not weaken the base package-role requirements.
Inventing atomic units, objectives, or content is invalid because it breaks grounding and corrupts downstream work.
Nested partitions are invalid because they break flat partition invariants and complicate automation.
Silent ambiguity resolution is invalid because it hides defects and makes later reconciliation impossible.
Missing stable IDs are invalid because they prevent tracking and longitudinal comparison.
A missing Decomposition Ledger is invalid because it prevents machine-checkable coverage.
Missing Coverage & Telemetry is invalid because it prevents anti-fragile feedback over revisions.
Undeclared package roles are invalid because downstream agents cannot distinguish authoritative surfaces from derived artifacts.
A monolithic main document embedding heavy companion truth is invalid because it inflates the control surface and makes targeted retrieval and narrow diffs harder.
A monolithic main document embedding heavy companion truth is invalid because it invites parity failures with companion registers.
Conforming agents may add domain-specific anti-patterns but must not remove base anti-patterns.
STRUCTURE defines the abstract entity schemas and required output sections.
Conforming agents bind abstract schemas to domain-specific names and may add domain-specific fields.
An Atomic Unit has a stable UnitID in a format defined by the conforming agent.
An Atomic Unit has a normalized atomic statement.
An Atomic Unit has an InOutStatus value of IN, OUT, or TBD.
An Atomic Unit has a SourceRef, with TBD allowed on a best-effort basis.
An Atomic Unit has Notes.
An Objective has a stable ObjectiveID using the OBJ-NNN format.
An Objective has a statement.
An Objective has Notes.
An Objective has best-effort MappedProductionUnits, and empty mappings must be flagged.
A Partition has a stable PartitionID in a format defined by the conforming agent.
A Partition has a name.
A Partition has a scope description.
A Partition may have inclusion criteria.
A Partition may have exclusions.
A Production Unit has a stable ProductionUnitID mechanically coupled to ParentPartitionID.
A Production Unit has a name.
A Production Unit has a ParentPartitionID.
A Production Unit has a description.
A Production Unit has a ResponsibleParty, with TBD allowed.
A Production Unit has a Type from the domain-specific taxonomy defined by the conforming agent.
A Production Unit has an AnticipatedArtifacts list, with TBD allowed.
A Production Unit has CoversUnits using best-effort atomic unit IDs.
A Production Unit has SupportsObjectives using best-effort objective IDs.
Conforming agents may add fields such as ContextEnvelope or CanonicalSchema.
Added domain-specific fields must not conflict with the base schema.
An Artifact may have a stable ArtifactID.
An Artifact has a name.
An Artifact has a ParentProductionUnitID.
An Artifact has a Type from the domain-specific taxonomy defined by the conforming agent.
An Artifact has Notes.
Every conforming agent output must include the required Decomposition Document sections.
The order of required Decomposition Document sections is recommended but not mandatory.
A conforming Decomposition Document includes a Vocabulary Map table.
The Vocabulary Map table includes a CanonicalTerm column.
The Vocabulary Map table includes a Synonyms column.
The Vocabulary Map table includes a Notes column.
A conforming Decomposition Document includes a Decomposition Ledger table.
The Decomposition Ledger table includes a UnitID column.
The Decomposition Ledger table includes an InOutStatus column.
The Decomposition Ledger table includes a UnitStatement column.
The Decomposition Ledger table includes a SourceRef column.
The Decomposition Ledger table includes a PartitionID column that is required for IN rows and blank for OUT rows.
The Decomposition Ledger table includes ProductionUnitID values that may be one, many, or TBD.
The Decomposition Ledger table includes ObjectiveID values that may be zero, many, or TBD.
The Decomposition Ledger table may include a DecisionRef pointing to a Decision Log entry.
The Decomposition Ledger table includes an OpenIssue value of TRUE or FALSE.
The Decomposition Ledger table includes Notes.
Every IN-scope UnitID must have exactly one PartitionID.
Conforming agents may use domain-specific column names in the Decomposition Ledger.
The invariant structural contract is that every IN unit maps to exactly one partition.
A conforming Decomposition Document includes a Coverage & Telemetry summary block.
The Coverage & Telemetry summary includes UnitCount.
The Coverage & Telemetry summary includes PartitionCount.
The Coverage & Telemetry summary includes ProductionUnitCount.
The Coverage & Telemetry summary includes ObjectiveCount.
The Coverage & Telemetry summary includes UnassignedINUnits, which must be 0 for acceptance.
The Coverage & Telemetry summary includes a count of UnitsWithoutProductionUnitMapping.
The Coverage & Telemetry summary includes a count of UnmappedObjectives.
The Coverage & Telemetry summary includes OpenIssuesByType counts with IDs.
The Coverage & Telemetry summary includes a revision identifier and date.
Conforming agents may add domain-specific telemetry fields but must not omit the base telemetry fields.
A conforming Decomposition Document includes an Open Issues list of unresolved items referencing stable IDs.
A conforming Decomposition Document includes a Decision Log or Change Log.
The Decision Log or Change Log records non-trivial assignment and boundary decisions so later work can trace rationale.
A new decomposition agent instruction file that conforms to this specification must satisfy the extension contract.
A conforming agent instruction file must reference AGENT_DECOMP_BASE.md and state conformance to it.
A conforming agent instruction file must bind Source Corpus, Atomic Unit, Partition, Production Unit, and Artifact to domain-specific terms.
A conforming agent instruction file must define stable ID formats and widths for partitions, production units, and atomic units.
A conforming agent instruction file must define the production-unit type taxonomy.
A conforming agent instruction file must extend each of the 7 phases with domain-specific actions, outputs, and gate language.
A conforming agent instruction file must declare WRITE_SCOPE.
A conforming agent instruction file must add domain-specific fields, anti-patterns, and SPEC requirements as needed without replacing the base.
A conforming agent instruction file must declare domain-specific telemetry fields beyond the base Coverage & Telemetry schema.
A conforming agent instruction file must declare package architecture for authoritative working surfaces, companion registers, and derived publication artifacts.
A conforming agent instruction file must include a companion inventory section in the main decomposition document.
A conforming agent should include domain-specific rationale explaining why extensions exist.
A conforming agent should document deviations from the base specification with explicit justification.
The decomposition protocol for intake, normalization, partitioning, operationalization, verification, and publication is broadly invariant across domains.
PROJECT_DECOMP, SOFTWARE_DECOMP, and DOMAIN_DECOMP share the precedence order, invariants, required sections, completeness requirements, and consistency requirements.
A conforming variant may omit a phase when the domain ontology does not give that phase meaningful semantics.
Phase omissions and related entity, gate, or telemetry deviations must be explicitly documented in the variant doctrine with rationale.
DOMAIN_DECOMP omits the Objectives layer because domain knowledge handbooks rarely state explicit decomposable objectives.
DOMAIN_DECOMP absorbs principles, goals, and intent into Knowledge Types of Guidance / Playbook schema.
Remaining differences across variants are domain-specific semantics such as entity names, ID formats, type taxonomies, and domain-specific constraints.
Extracting the invariant protocol into a base specification reduces duplication by defining the shared contract once.
Extracting the invariant protocol into a base specification makes conformance auditable.
Extracting the invariant protocol into a base specification clarifies what is invariant and what is domain-specific.
Extracting the invariant protocol into a base specification supports future variants that inherit the protocol with domain-specific extensions.
Domain-specific content that cannot be abstracted without losing meaning stays in concrete variants.
Entity names and ID formats stay in concrete variants.
Type taxonomies and canonical schemas stay in concrete variants.
Phase-level actions specific to a domain stay in concrete variants.
Domain-specific sizing constraints stay in concrete variants.
Domain-specific anti-patterns stay in concrete variants.
WRITE_SCOPE varies by domain purpose and stays in concrete variants.
Downstream pipeline references stay in concrete variants.
